key_agronomy_tips: Ensure standing water (2-5 cm) during tillering to panicle initiation. Critical stages: CRI, tillering, panicle emergence.
Crown Root Initiation (CRI) at 21 days after sowing is the most critical irrigation stage. Avoid late sowing to prevent terminal heat.
source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat & Barley Research (IIWBR)

key_agronomy_tips: Very sensitive to waterlogging. Ridges and furrow planting recommended. Critical stages: Tasseling and silking.
Stake indeterminate varieties. Maintain uniform soil moisture to avoid Blossom End Rot caused by calcium deficiency.
Requires long frost-free period and sunny weather during boll opening. Critical stages: Square formation and boll development.

soil_type: Well-aerated sandy loam to clay loam
key_agronomy_tips: Avoid excessive vegetative growth caused by over-irrigation. Critical stages: Pre-flowering and pod development. Inoculate with Rhizobium.
Apply gypsum (400 kg/ha) at pegging stage (40-45 DAS) for uniform pod filling and calcium supply.
First irrigation at 30-35 DAS (flowering stage). Thinning within 15-20 DAS is essential to maintain optimal plant population.
